I've been trying to get a basic understanding of DFT, but I'm not sure how to get into it...everyone I know seems to use some kind of software package to do it...do you have any suggestions?

Abinit, CP2K and Quantum Espresso are software packages I know of that are open source. I have no idea how user-friendly they are though, especially if someone doesn't fully know what they're doing.

I suggest starting off by understanding the Hohenberg-Kohn theorems, and what exactly an exchange-correlation functional is. And (roughly) what LDA and GGA are.

If you like programming, you could try writing a Hartree-Fock code to get a feel for what constitutes a quantum chemistry code.

This is a good review paper.

And I've heard great things about "Density Functional Theory: A Practical Introduction" by Scholl & Steckel.

Sadly, as far as I know, there are very few software packages with good manuals.
